final_answer:
MEMORANDUM
To: David Herrera, General Counsel, Vellura Therapeutics. Re: Anand / Novacel - trade secret and restrictive covenant enforcement options. Analysis is keyed to the record through May 26, 2025; if read later, the 12-month covenant period (to May 16, 2026) may have run.

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) Lead with trade secret and contract claims against Anand (DTSA, Massachusetts Trade Secrets Act (MTSA), breach of EICA s.2.4/4.2, SCTSA s.4(c)/5, fiduciary duty), filed in Massachusetts federal or Suffolk Superior Court (Business Litigation Session) now, before he or Novacel files in California. (b) Seek a narrow TRO/PI: preservation, non-use/non-disclosure, return and neutral forensic imaging of the USB drive, Gmail and devices, and expedited discovery. Do not lead with a bar on working at Novacel. (c) Plead the non-compete in the alternative; it is exposed on three fronts: Mass. G.L. c.149 s.24L technical compliance, California law, and DTSA limits on employment injunctions. (d) Novacel is a harder defendant (California; no contract; no evidence yet of receipt or use). Send a preservation/notice letter, and sue after expedited discovery or in California. (e) The forensic story is strong, but record inconsistencies and control gaps must be fixed before anyone signs a declaration.

2. FACTS AND RECORD PROBLEMS TO RESOLVE
Core facts (forensic report): 2,347 files (4.8 GB) to a personal USB in 14 sessions, Mar 15-Apr 28, 2025 (312 Trade Secret/Highly Confidential); 17 emails to his Gmail, Apr 1-25; Saturday Apr 26 lab entry 11:47 PM-2:13 AM with a 341-file session; Feb 10-Mar 5 searches on Novacel and California non-compete law; Jan 22 dinner with Novacel's CEO; resignation May 2; Separation Certification May 14; Novacel CSO announcement May 19.
Inconsistencies a defense lawyer will exploit:
- Certification content. The report says Anand certified deletion of personal-device data and initialed each representation. The actual signed form (HR-SC-003) has no deletion representation, and paragraphs 1-2 say property/documents "have returned, or will return" by May 16, so they are not flatly false. The strongest false statements are para. 3 (has not retained copies, including USB and personal email) and para. 4 (no transfer to third parties; unproven). Use the actual signed document.
- Laptop return: May 14 (report) vs May 16 (exit interview).
- Classification counts: report 147 Trade Secret/165 Highly Confidential/1,412 Internal/623 Public; access-log workbook 214/98/147/0 (459 total) and says Aurora appeared in 3 of 17 emails (report: 4). About 87% of downloaded files were Internal or Public. Either reconcile or define the 312 by file list.
- Controls: the report says no email DLP exists; the policy (s.4.3) says DLP scans outbound mail; the workbook says a DLP rule "triggered but log-only." The report says VPs had no after-hours alerts; the policy (s.5.1) gives VPs standing after-hours access, so April 26 access was authorized (the issue is the downloads, not entry).
- Identifiers differ across documents: employee ID, laptop model/tag, email domain, Montoya's title, "Top Secret" vs "Trade Secret."
- March 15, 2025 was a Saturday, yet the report says April 26 was the only weekend activity. Check whether March 15 was remote or on-site.
- Salary is $385,000 in both 2020 and 2025; confirm highest base in the prior two years (it sets garden leave).

3. TRADE SECRET STATUS AND REASONABLE MEASURES
DTSA (18 U.S.C. s.1839(3)) and MTSA require valuable, not generally known information subject to reasonable secrecy measures. Strong: VelluSphere compositions VS-FORM-001 to 014, Aurora data (six SCTSA categories), process parameters, unpublished patent drafts (secrecy ends on publication), unannounced pipeline, supplier pricing. Weaker: partly disclosed clinical data, Internal/Public files, and Anand's general skill (EICA Art. 5). Identify secrets by file list; California (CCP s.2019.210) and many federal judges require particularity.
Measures: classification tiers, RBAC, MFA, audit logs, training (last Nov 8, 2024), NDAs, badge control, exit protocol. Gaps: log-only USB monitoring despite a policy that bans personal USB "at all times"; no block or alert; policy-promised monthly anomaly reports (50+ files, 500 MB+ sessions, Tier 4 transfers) apparently produced no action in March-April; notice-of-resignation steps (s.7.1: 90-day access report, USB escalation) not documented after May 2; DLP uncertainty. The standard is reasonable, not perfect, measures, and the taker was a trusted insider, so courts often find them adequate; expect discovery on why the monthly reports were ignored.
Misappropriation theory: acquisition by "improper means" includes breach of a duty to maintain secrecy (s.1839(6)); downloading to personal media violated EICA s.2.4 and SCTSA s.4(c) even though system access was authorized. Use is not yet shown; the case rests on acquisition plus threatened use (his role, concealment, false certification).

4. CLAIMS (ranked)
1. DTSA/MTSA vs Anand: acquisition, threatened use/disclosure. Remedies include injunction, damages, and exemplary damages (2x) and fees; the agreements contain the s.1833(b) immunity notice, preserving those remedies.
2. Breach of contract (EICA, SCTSA, ENCNSA s.5): simplest; perpetual confidentiality; fee-shifting (SCTSA s.7; ENCNSA s.7.2).
3. Breach of fiduciary duty/duty of loyalty (VP, CEO's direct report): preparing to compete is lawful, but taking confidential information is not (Chelsea Indus. v. Gaffney, 389 Mass. 1 (1983)).
4. Non-compete and non-solicit (ENCNSA): see section 5.
5. Novacel: MTSA/DTSA misappropriation (needs knowledge or reason to know), tortious interference with contract, c.93A s.11 (needs conduct "primarily and substantially" in Massachusetts; doubtful). No evidence yet of Novacel's knowledge; a notice letter creates it going forward.
6. Fraud on the certification: weak as a tort (no reliance); use as intent evidence and for the 24-month trigger. CFAA: weak after Van Buren v. United States, 593 U.S. 374 (2021) (authorized access, misused); omit. 

5. ENCNSA ENFORCEABILITY (Mass. G.L. c.149 s.24L, agreements on or after Oct 1, 2018)
Favorable: two signatories, counsel-consultation language, notice recital, consideration beyond continued employment (promotion, $50,000 bonus, garden leave), voluntary resignation, Massachusetts law and Suffolk forum (s.24L(e)-(f): he lived and worked in Massachusetts before separation), reformation power (s.24L(d); ENCNSA s.10.3). The 24-month term is available only if Vellura proves breach of fiduciary duty or unlawful taking of property (s.1.5, burden on Vellura); the forensic record supports that, otherwise 12 months. Non-solicits are outside s.24L's definition of non-competes, so garden leave defects do not void them (ENCNSA ss.3, 4.5).
Weaknesses:
- Garden leave. Payments were wired May 26 (covering May 17-31); ENCNSA s.4.2 allows commencement within 30 days (by about June 15), so the delay is likely not a breach, and the statement that delay "voids" the covenant overstates; but an early letter and prompt payment help. Keep paying biweekly without gaps. Section 24L(b)(vii) requires at least 50% of highest base paid pro rata for the whole restricted period and bars the employer from unilaterally discontinuing payments except upon employee breach. ENCNSA s.4.3 (election not to enforce within 30 days) and s.4.4 (offset down to 25%) are in tension with that and with the 50% floor. Do not invoke either. I could not retrieve the statute text directly; quotations come from secondary summaries; verify against the official text. Although s.7.3 and the statute permit cessation on breach, continue paying under written reservation of rights to recoup until a court rules.
- Scope. "Competing Enterprise" is enterprise-wide and nationwide-plus; s.24L presumes reasonable only restrictions tied to services performed in the prior two years and territories where he worked. Section 2.1(a) (any role) is overbroad; 2.1(b) (same or similar services) is defensible. Expect reformation, not voidance.
- Proof of notice: locate evidence of delivery 10 business days before March 1, 2020 and Anand's signature (copies reviewed are unsigned forms).
- Prior non-enforcement (Osei 2021 to MIT; Ramirez 2023 to non-competing pharma): ENCNSA s.10.4 has a non-waiver clause, and the departures differ in kind, but undocumented decisions and no board record invite waiver/selective-enforcement arguments. Prepare declarations now; do not create backdated memos.
Net: a Massachusetts court would likely enforce a reformed covenant; timing is the constraint.

6. CALIFORNIA
Anand lives in La Jolla and works for a San Diego employer. California B&P s.16600 voids non-competes (Edwards v. Arthur Andersen, 44 Cal.4th 937 (2008)); s.16600.5 (SB 699, effective Jan 1, 2024) declares them void wherever signed, bars employers from attempting enforcement, and creates a private action with fees. A California court will likely refuse to enforce the Massachusetts clause. Risks of suing in Massachusetts on the non-compete: a retaliatory California declaratory/s.16600.5 suit (fee exposure); first-filed comity is helpful but not controlling (Advanced Bionics v. Medtronic, 29 Cal.4th 697 (2002), declined to let a California court enjoin the parallel out-of-state action but kept its own case alive). Whether s.16600.5 reaches a Massachusetts suit is unsettled. Mitigate: file first, plead the non-compete count last and in the alternative, and make trade secrets the basis for relief.
DTSA injunctions may not "prevent a person from entering into an employment relationship," must rest on "evidence of threatened misappropriation and not merely on the information the person knows," and may not conflict with state law restraining lawful trades (18 U.S.C. s.1836(b)(3)(A)(i)). California rejects inevitable disclosure (Whyte v. Schlage Lock, 101 Cal.App.4th 1443 (2002)). So seek conduct-based relief (non-use, return, forensics); consider limits on his LNP work only if discovery shows use. Threatened misappropriation rests on retained copies plus concealment, not the Novacel job.

7. FORUM
Anand consented to exclusive Massachusetts jurisdiction (EICA s.8.1, ENCNSA s.8.2; SCTSA s.8.1), so personal jurisdiction is secure. D. Mass. (Suffolk County, Boston) offers federal-question jurisdiction (DTSA) with supplemental MTSA and contract claims, and satisfies the Suffolk clause; Suffolk Superior Court's Business Litigation Session is the alternative. Novacel is not bound by the forum clause; Massachusetts jurisdiction over it is contestable, so S.D. Cal. is safer. TRO standard: likelihood of success, irreparable harm, balance of hardships, public interest (Winter v. NRDC, 555 U.S. 7 (2008); state: Packaging Indus. Grp. v. Cheney, 380 Mass. 609 (1980)). Delay since May 16 erodes urgency; move this week. The Stored Communications Act blocks civil subpoenas to Google for Gmail content; seek an order directed to Anand.

8. EVIDENCE AND PRIVILEGE
The forensic report is labeled privileged and work product, but it states it arose from the "standard post-departure protocol" (policy s.7.3 requires it), the exit interview HR note (itself not privileged) recommended it on May 14, and it will be needed to prove the case. Expect a waiver/at-issue fight. Plan: a factual declaration authenticating logs; retain an outside forensic firm to re-verify hashes, the USB serial and the March 15 and April 26 sessions. Preserve: images, logs, video (90-day retention; April 26 footage expires about July 25, 2025, so confirm export), Montoya notes, Osei/Ramirez files, observer agreement, expense reports. Extend the hold to Facilities, Finance, Ruiz, Watanabe and the Steering Committee that chose log-only. Conflicts: Whitfield & Crane drafted the agreements; if s.24L defects emerge, consider independent review. The GC approved the ENCNSA and made the Ramirez decision, so he is a fact witness.

9. DESHMUKH / RIDGELINE
Observer Q2 2019-Q4 2022 under a confidentiality agreement; her material (strategy, pipeline, early roadmap) is stale and high-level, and Aurora began in 2023. No evidence of transmission. No claim now. Send a preservation request, gather the observer agreement and the January 2025 conference/dinner attendance, and revisit after Anand's and Novacel's discovery.

10. RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE
1. Today: confirm payments schedule and Anand's highest base; hold notice supplements; export video.
2. Within 48 hours: reconcile section 2 discrepancies; retain forensic consultant; draft verified complaint and TRO papers.
3. Same day as filing: serve a demand on Anand (return, non-use, certify, preserve, produce devices); send preservation/notice letters to Novacel (and to Forsythe) and to Anand's counsel; ask for stipulated forensic protocol. A letter-only first step invites a California filing or deletion.
4. Seek expedited discovery on Novacel contacts, Gmail, USB, and personal devices; evaluate adding Novacel (S.D. Cal. or D. Mass.) on the results.
5. Remediate controls (USB block mode, DLP, anomaly alerts).
6. Audit Committee briefing: trade secret claims against Anand strong; non-compete moderate in Massachusetts, weak in California; Novacel unproven.
Damages: the $85 million valuation measures asset value, not loss; plan expert work on unjust enrichment.
Open items: signed originals; 2020 notice delivery; cyber insurance; Anand's counsel.
